correctness.rationale: For all odd integers n>=5, Q_n is full-dimensional and its 2n coordinate/edge inequalities are facets. The finite Fourier average F_n(t) is strictly monotone in the required H_n(t); its unique root is equivalent by a Poisson root-of-unity filter to 1-4q-q^2=q^n(1+4q-q^2), q in (0,sqrt5-2). The circulant inverse D=(I+tA_n/2)^(-1) is positive definite; D_ii=F_n, and F_n+tD_i,i+1=1 yield Sigma_ii=a^2 and (e_i+e_i+1)^T Sigma(e_i+e_i+1)=(1-2a)^2. Hence E is contained in Q_n and tangent to all 2n facets. Positive weights 2a on -e_i and 1-2a on e_i+e_i+1 obey the normalized zero first moment and full Sigma^(-1) second moment, which proves unique global John optimality. Fourier diagonalization yields positive principal eigenvalues eta/[1+t cos(2pi j/n)]; the cyclotomic product gives the displayed determinant and exact volume. The factored root gap gives (1/sqrt5-t_n)/(sqrt5-2)^n -> 8sqrt5/25. Independent symbolic algebra verified exact equivalence to the published general fractional-matching formula; a separate high-precision numerical checker sampled nine odd dimensions (5,7,9,11,13,21,31,51,101), seven full shape/contact/John/determinant cases (n<=31), and the asymptotic scaled limit. The infinite theorem rests on analytic steps, not numerical sampling.

The positive contact-weight argument requires exact scalar normalization, which was reconstructed algebraically rather than inferred from a verifier exit code.

originality.rationale: The principal all-odd-cycle John-ellipsoid, all-facet contact, eigenvalue and volume classification is already a literal specialization (under an edge-coordinate relabeling) of the published general theorem “Spectral John ellipsoids of vertex-and-edge-transitive fractional matching polytopes.” For G=C_n the edge coordinates of F_G obey x_e>=0 and x_{e-1}+x_e<=1, exactly Q_n; B^T B=2I+A_n. The general theorem also explicitly states the cycle golden-ratio parameter limit. The submitted sharp leading exponential coefficient is not printed there, but follows by a short root-of-unity filter and Taylor expansion from its exact finite-cycle spectral equation. It is a mathematically correct subordinate quantitative refinement, not a distinct uncaptured principal theorem as submitted.
